newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA's Guisti denies Saudi oil output threats.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA's Guisti denies Saudi oil output threats.

text.p: Luis Giusti, president of Venezuela's state owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), denied on Tuesday a report that Saudi Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman threatened Venezuela with an oil output hike if it continued to violate its agreed supply quota.

The threat was reported in the Wall Street Journal on August 14, but Giusti said the private conversation at last year's OPEC meeting had been cordial and they had discussed possible joint-ventures in refining and marketing.
Giusti's denial follows a previous denial by the prince, a nephew of Saudi King Fahd and a deputy oil minister.

"Saudi Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman hinted at a private meeting with Mr Giusti that Saudi Arabia might raise production itself to drive down prices and punish the Venezuelans," the Wall Street Journal reported.

Venezuela is a founder member of the Organization for Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), but has become the focus of criticism by Saudi Arabia, Iran and other members for producing well above its agreed quota.

But Saudi Arabia has been particularly careful not to indicate that it would increase its production in retaliation after an attempt in the mid-1980s to regain lost market share led to a price collapse.
